title: Nonuniform prefill affinity and subtoken reuse orchestrator
creator: Sofia Huang
description: Problem statement: As workloads diversify (short chit-chat, long-form assistants, and code completions) our paged-attention KV cache sees highly nonuniform access patterns. Current single-policy prefill/evict heuristics cause suboptimal kernel selection and increased decode tail latency for interactive tails. Goals: 1) Reduce 95th/99th decode latency for mixed workloads by prioritizing prefill admission using a nonuniform affinity score that combines tenant usage pattern, token subtypes (natural language vs. code), and predicted reuse windows. 2) Introduce a lightweight 'subtoken reuse' tag that groups contiguous subtokens from the same conversation/model path so the runtime can co-locate and prefer reuse-friendly kernels. 3) Provide an orchestrator that ties affinity -> admission -> kernel hedging decisions so prefill/evict choices steer kernel selection early in the decode pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 95th decode latency reduced by >= 12% on mixed workload benchmark (short + long + code) compared to baseline prefill policy
KV reuse hit-rate increases by >= 8% for high-reuse tenants in lab traces
Kernel selection logs show a reduction in cross-kernel fallbacks during first 50 decode tokens for prioritized prefill requests
No regression in median latency or token throughput on synthetic load (within 3%)
Design doc and public-facing runbook updated; runtime feature gated behind 'nonuniform_prefill' flag
